To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the neutral ZrL(4) complexes of oxine, tropolonate, and ethyl maltol have been successfully synthesized and characterized, and the oxinate complex has been used to radiolabel human cancer cells.
a range of lipophilic zirconium(iv)-based complexes have been prepared, characterized, evaluated and shown to be suitable for cell labelling with (89)Zrfour.
a series of ZrL4 complexes have been synthesised for cell labelling with the long half-life PET nuclide Zr-89.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a range of neutral lipophilic Zr(IV) complexes for cell lab labelling and positron emission tomographic imaging using the long half-life (89)Zirconium.
the preparation of lipophilic Zr(IV) complexes of oxine, tropolonate or ethyl maltolate for use in cell tracking studies with (89)Zirconium.
the development of Zr(iv) complexes as radiopharmaceuticals for cell labelling with Zr- 89.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the (89)Zirconium(IV) complexes of the ligands oxine, tropolonate, and ethyl maltol are promising candidates for further evaluation as cell labelling agents for positron emission tomographic imaging.
(89) Zr(oxinate)(4) has been prepared and evaluated for labelling cells and is a promising candidate for cell tracking by positron emission computed tomography.
(89) Zr(oxinate)(4) is the most promising of the complexes for cell tracking and that (89)zirconium(iv) tropolonate and (89)Zirconium(iv) ethyl maltolate are not promising candidates.

the oxinate and tropolate ligands have been successfully used for the preparation of Zr(IV) complexes for cell labeling with (89)Zrfollowing the same synthetic procedure.
we have shown that the oxinate and tropolone complexes of (89) Zr are promising candidates for cell labelling, but that the ethyl maltolate complex is unsuitable.
(89)89Zr(oxinates)4 is a promising candidate for cell tracking by positron emission computed tomography.
